- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.4) or shows strong downward momentum, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects in next 3–7 days; apply downward bias of 2–5% for 3–7 days post-spike.  
- If true price deviates from 30-day moving average by >2%, model often fails to revert; apply mean reversion bias toward 30-day MA for next 7–14 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.7 → 0.3 → 0.7), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment swing midpoint for next 5–10 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if model’s first 3–5 days are significantly above true, reduce early forecast by 2–5% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is high but price drops sharply (e.g., >3% in 3 days), model often fails to anticipate; add 1–3% downward bias for next 7 days.
